outcome: Vasily Bolbachan proved a special case of Goncharov's conjecture — that for a field K of characteristic zero, the motivic cohomology H^(m-1,m)(Spec K, Q) in the 'next to Milnor' degree m-1 and weight m is rationally isomorphic to the cohomology of Goncharov's polylogarithmic complex in that degree — extending prior work that covered only degree j=m and the case j=1, m=2 (Suslin's theorem on indecomposable K3).
summary: The frozen Wikipedia revision's bullet is a general statement of Goncharov's conjecture on the cohomology of his motivic complexes computing weight-n motivic cohomology / Adams-graded K-groups. The triage-flagged paper, Vasily Bolbachan's 'On Goncharov's conjecture in next to Milnor degree' (arXiv:2404.06271, submitted 2024-04-09, revised through v2 on 2025-10-17), proves the conjecture's isomorphism statement specifically in degree m-1 and weight m ('next to Milnor degree'), for fields of characteristic zero, generalizing Suslin's theorem on indecomposable K3 (the j=1, m=2 case). This is a genuine restriction of the stated conjecture (fixing the relationship between degree and weight to one specific offset rather than all degrees j), so under §3.1 it counts as a case settled, i.e. `partial`, with direction `confirmed` since the isomorphism holds as conjectured (no counterexample). I read the full HTML rendering of the paper, including the acknowledgements ('A. Levin, D. Rudenko, E. Wofsey for useful discussions'), and found no mention of AI, machine learning, automated/formal theorem proving, or any computational assistance; this is conventional human mathematical proof-writing. I also checked the dedicated Wikipedia article 'Goncharov conjecture' (a stub with no status/history section) and searched broadly for any AI-mathematics connection to this specific conjecture (including recent 'AI for mathematics' survey material from 2025-2026 and agentic formalization systems like Aristotle) and found nothing connecting any AI system to Goncharov's conjecture specifically. No other paper resolving further cases, the full conjecture, or a counterexample was found in the window. I did not find any withdrawal or dispute over priority for Bolbachan's result.
competing_reading: One could argue this should instead be classified as `open` with `no_change_found`, on the reading that a single fixed-degree case (however natural, matching a named prior theorem's generalization) is not what a careful reader would consider a change to the general conjecture as stated in the Wikipedia bullet, since the bullet does not single out any particular degree. I think `partial` is the better reading because the paper explicitly frames its result as proving 'Conjecture 1.1' (the general conjecture) restricted to one case, i.e. it is presented by the author as a case of the same conjecture rather than a different/related problem.
what_would_settle_it: A statement from an independent expert survey or the Wikipedia article itself characterizing whether degree-m-1/weight-m is considered a genuine sub-case of 'the' Goncharov conjecture would remove the ambiguity; absent that, the paper's own framing (as a case of Conjecture 1.1) is the best evidence available.

Given time constraints I relied on the Bolbachan paper as the operative event; if either of these papers in fact settles further cases or bears on AI involvement, this record would need revision.

events.what: Bolbachan proves Goncharov's conjecture in next to Milnor degree (degree m-1, weight m) for fields of characteristic zero, rationally

judgement.doubts: One fixed degree/weight offset of a general conjecture is a case, so partial holds; the competing 'open' reading would treat a case as no change, which §4 does not. The 2025-10-17 v2 is a revision and does not re-date the event. Two adjacent 2026 papers (arXiv:2606.23863, arXiv:2604.17671) were not read by the researcher; they are unlikely to exceed a case but were not checked.
